title: Staged Rollout Safety & Validation Runner for LTS and Minor Upgrades
creator: Aisha Mendez
description: Build an automated runner that composes and executes a staged validation workflow for rolling upgrades across LTS and non-LTS channels. The runner should orchestrate lightweight smoke checks, targeted performance regression gates, and a compact eval-suite tied to known customer-critical prompts before advancing each rollout stage (canary -> gradated -> full). The goal is to prevent regressions that increase tail latency or lower quality for high-volume routes while keeping validation time under configurable SLOs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A runnable pipeline (CI job + ad-hoc CLI) that executes smoke, perf, and eval steps and returns a single pass/fail decision per stage.
2) Thresholds and metrics configurable per release channel (LTS vs minor).
3) Integration with release orchestration to block stage promotion on failure and emit structured failure reasons.
4) Dashboard tiles and alerting hooks for failures within 5 minutes of run completion.
5) End-to-end run time < 45 minutes for standard canary matrix (50k tokens of synthetic traffic + 5 eval prompts).
test_plan:
- Smoke: service sanity (API health, key endpoints) + small synthetic workload (1000 requests across routes).
- Perf gate: compare p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput against baseline snapshot; fail on >12% regression in p95 or >18% in p99 for routes labeled 'latency-sensitive'.
- Eval-suite: 20 curated prompts across classification/generation/structured-output; compare quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity) against baseline with a 2% absolute drop threshold for core routes.
- KV cache warmup validation and token-cost regression check.
- Optional: run dark traffic sample replay for long-tail token patterns if run mode == 'extended'.
run_steps:
1. Kick off pipeline via CI or console release action.
2. Provision ephemeral test cluster (or use dedicated validation pool) with pinned image.
3. Run smoke battery; collect logs and basic telemetry.
4. If smoke passes, run perf gate harness (load generator + latency collection).
5. If perf gate passes, run compact eval-suite and compute diffs vs baseline.
6. Upload artifacts (traces, histograms, eval reports) to release dashboard, then emit promote/block decision.
7. On block, automatically create a rollback alert and link relevant artifacts and a checklist for oncall.
automation_notes:
- Leverage existing preload snapshot infra from ENG-10824 for baseline collection.
- Use model-compatibility prober (lightweight binary) to validate KV cache and kernel selection behaviors before perf run.
- Support dry-run mode to exercise runner without blocking actual promotion.
- Runner should tag artifacts with channel: {lts,stable,canary} and release id.
observability_and_alerting:
- Dashboard: release/validation/<release-id> with pass/fail, run duration, p95 delta, eval score delta.
- Alerts: Slack + PagerDuty for fails on LTS channel; email for non-LTS.
- Store artifacts in s3://redwood-release-artifacts/<release-id>/validation/<run-id>.
- Correlate with Console traces and cost telemetry (token counts).
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Running full evals on every canary slows cadence; mitigated via compact eval-suite and sample sizes.
- False positives from noisy perf regressions (infra variability): mitigate with repeated runs and confidence intervals, and require 2/3 failing windows before final block.
- Cost of ephemeral clusters vs risk of missed regressions: prioritize LTS/major releases for extended validations.
updates: 2026-02-13: Project kickoff. Drafted initial acceptance criteria and test plan. Assigned Derek for implementation and Aisha for release coordination.
2026-02-20: Spike: prototyped smoke + perf gate using small internal cluster. Baseline p95 collection working. Added dependency on ENG-10824 for baseline snapshot automation.
2026-02-27: Design review with SRE and Console teams. Decided to surface validation artifacts in Console under release details. Action: Console ticket to add artifact tab (PM to prioritize).
2026-03-01: Implemented perf gate harness and integrated with CI; initial threshold tuned: p95 delta 12% / p99 18% for latency-sensitive routes. Running overnight A/B to reduce noise.

2026-03-05: First end-to-end run against runtime-1.22 candidate. Smoke passed; perf gate had intermittent p99 blips due to noisy infra. Added repeated-run logic (3 attempts) and statistical check. Next: add compact eval-suite scoring and Console integration.
2026-03-05 (note): Blocker identified — dedicated validation pool lacks autoscaling for short bursts. Filed ENG-39510 to add burst capacity.
comments: Derek Huang: Need to decide whether the runner itself should be a service or a set of orchestrated CI jobs. My leaning: keep it as CI-first with a simple CLI for ad-hoc runs to avoid long-lived infra ops.
Priya Rao (SRE): Perf noise is our main concern — suggest using performance-canary nodes isolated from tenant traffic for the perf gate to reduce variance.
Nate Flores (PM): Important to tie 'customer_impact' metadata to the routes we test; will provide a prioritized route list for the eval-suite by 2026-03-08.
Design: Console UX should expose run artifacts and allow re-run from UI; refer to design mock in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/RELEASE-DESIGN/validation-ui-mock.png
